name: Timor-Leste
why: Facebook and Google Maps; very little else is indexed.

spots.name: Nino Konis National Park
spots.desc: Established in 2007 and named after resistance fighter Nino Konis Santana (1957-1998) who was born in Tutuala, this park of 1,236 km2 covers six subdistricts including Tutuala and the seas outside. The park protects both nature and the cultural and historical heritage of the region. This includes coral reefs and the largest intact rainforest in the region with countless orchid species.…

spots.name: Motael Church
spots.local: Igreja de Santo António de Motael
spots.desc: The oldest church in Timor-Leste. Originally from around 1800, the current building dates to 1955. The church played an important role in the independence struggle. In 1991, when independence activists demonstrated against the Indonesian occupation, they were offered protection in the church. At night, the Indonesians stormed the church and shot activist Sebastião Gomes. After his memorial…

spots.name: Berau
spots.desc: Berau is a small village on the island's south coast. It is home to the island's only freshwater spring, which also supplies drinking water to Maquili, Vila, Beloi, and Biquili. With advance planning, you can rent a boat to reach various spots in the area or explore the small cliffs. The small marine reserve is highly valued by divers for its rich biodiversity. The village has both a small…

spots.name: Vatuo
spots.desc: Vatuo is in the far north of Atauro's west coast. To reach it, you one either travel around the northern tip of the island or cross the island's interior and then head north. Approximately 200 people live here, most of whom are Protestant and not Catholic. The local initiative is particularly proud of the turtle nesting sites they protect. The village has no electricity, and water is a scarce…

spots.name: Adara
spots.desc: Adara lies on the west coast. Life in this village of fewer than 200 inhabitants is much quieter than on the east coast. A hammock overlooking the white sand beach is the perfect place to relax. The coral reef, perfect for snorkeling, is 50 meters from the beach. Adara is home to the Wawata Topu (meaning "female divers"): women who dive with simple swimming goggles and harpoons to fish and…

spots.name: Arlo
spots.desc: Arlo lies a little way from the coast in the mountains northwest of Atauro. The village has a population of just under 500. It's located on the road from the east coast to Adara and is worth a short stop for a fresh coconut. The route should be hiked in the early morning or late afternoon, not in the dark or during the heat of the day. While the route to Adara is lined with rocks, the path to…

spots.name: Beloi
spots.desc: Beloi is the port where most visitors arrive by ferry to the island. The arrival of the ships is used as an opportunity to operate a small market. With its lively atmosphere, it is somewhat vying with the sleepy Vila for the title of capital. Beloi is developing into the island's tourist center, offering accommodations, restaurants, and entertainment. While in Beloi, you should definitely take…

spots.name: Maquili
spots.desc: This fishing village lies about an hour's walk south of Vila, along a beautiful path along the rugged coastline. Maquili is known for its woodwork. Boats are built here (half-finished ones, still under construction, can be found here and there along the coast), and dance masks, as well as figures of men and women, are carved. There were also carvings of mermaids and eels, which are said to allude…

spots.name: Acrema
spots.desc: It is a quiet village, known primarily for its white sand beach. In addition, there are reefs with excellent diving opportunities. A two-hour walk from Biqueli, it's ideal for a day trip. The coastal road extends to this point in the far north of the east coast, so it's also possible to reach it by car. Maun Elias, the village chief (+670-7801-2661), is happy to give a tour of the village…

spots.name: Anartutu
spots.desc: It lies in Suco Macadade, in the southwest of the island, and is one of the more remote villages. As the highest settlement on the island, it already offers a beautiful view of the surrounding landscape below, and Mano Côco, Atauro's highest mountain, is not far from here. Few villages on Atauro are not located on the coast, and the inhabitants of Anartutu must make do with what they earn on the…

spots.name: Atecru
spots.desc: It takes about an hour to walk here from Adara, making it ideal for a day trip or as a stopover on a multi-day trek. It's one of the most beautiful spots on the island. Towards evening, the inhabitants search for marine life in the shallow tide pools. They have rediscovered their own culture, reviving old dances and games and speaking the local dialect. The village chiefs can tell ancient legends…

spots.name: Biqueli
spots.desc: Biqueli (Pala, Bikeli-Pala) is on the east coast. You can either hike there from Beloi in one to two hours, or hire a truck or motorcycle taxi to travel north on the island's main road. Hitchhiking is also an option, as virtually every passing truck will inevitably pass through Biqueli. The village has a hot (40°C) salt water spring, but it is too hot for bathing, except at high tide where the…

spots.name: Douro
spots.desc: Doro is in the northwest of Atauro. Ocean currents from the west and north converge off its coast. According to locals, one of the island's most biodiverse reefs is one of the best places to observe blacktip reef sharks.

spots.name: Iliana
spots.desc: It lies in the western hill country. From Biqueli, it can be reached on foot in three to four hours, or by motorcycle taxi. A road also leads here from Beloi. Away from the main village, inland, a few small huts lie on the beach where fishermen store their equipment.

spots.name: Uaro-Ana
spots.desc: It's a quiet village in the north of the east coast. It's definitely a good place to stop for a coconut on the way, an overnight stay with a host family, or some souvenirs from the small shop run by the local women 's cooperative. Hats, baskets, and wood carvings are cheaper here than in the main shop in Beloi. There's also a small Protestant church in the village.

spots.name: Santa Cruz cemetery
spots.desc: Site of the Santa Cruz massacre on 12 November 1991 when at least 250 Timorese were murdered after a funeral procession for activist Sebastião Gomes, who was shot in Motael Church. You can see the graves of Sebastião Gomes, as well as of British cameraman Max Stahl who had filmed the massacre and later requested to be buried here.

spots.name: Cristo Rei
spots.desc: The statue of Jesus that stands on a headland to the east of Dili. Rumour has it that, when the mainly Muslim Indonesians built the statue as a gift to the mainly Christian Timorese, they designed it so that Jesus would be facing towards Jakarta. The statue is about 20 metres tall and stands on a globe of earth. The route from Dili along the beach and up the steps to the Jesus statue is popular…

spots.name: Cape Fatucama
spots.desc: Aka Backside Beach. The beach directly behind the Jesus statue, it's a scenic, inverted c-shaped coastline with near-transparent waters much better than the one at Areia Branca. If driving, head east towards Baucau on the road that crosses the ridge near Ramos-Horta's house and look for the turnoff on the left. Otherwise, you walk up the steps towards Cristo Rei and then, halfway up, go down…

spots.name: Resistance Museum
spots.desc: Learn about the struggle for Timor-Leste's independence and what the people went through in the massive 25-year-long struggle.

spots.name: Dare War Memorial
spots.desc: A memorial to Sparrow Force, an Australian unit that fought the Japanese in Timor for several years, plus an exhibition on the unit and on the Timorese experience of the war. Good views over Dili and a café open on weekends.

spots.name: Chega! Exhibition
spots.desc: Set in a prison used during Portuguese and Indonesian times, you can visit the dark cells in which prisoners were held. There's also an exhibition on the struggle for independence and the persecution of Timorese people during the Indonesian occupation.

spots.name: Timor Plaza
spots.desc: The shopping mall in Dili. Good place for ATMs, SIM cards, souvenirs, ice cream, cinema, and Friday after work happy hour. 1.5 km east of the airport.

spots.name: Empreza Di'ak NGO Shop
spots.desc: A Timorese organisation that works on economical empowerment to build better futures. Here you can find beautiful handicrafts and traditional products from Timor-Leste.

spots.name: Arte Moris
spots.desc: Art centre that sells Timorese paintings, often painted directly on Tais. Recurring themes are local symbols and the life and death during the Indonesian occupation.

spots.name: Tais Market
spots.desc: A central place to pick up Tais, old coins, woodwork, pottery and other curios. Beware the imitation Tais, which are sometimes from Indonesia. There are a lot of stores with mostly identical offerings, so look around and choose a seller at random, or based on who wants to tell you about the regional differences. US$40-60 for a large tais (depending on how fancy it is), $30 for a medium tais.…

spots.name: Alola Esperansa
spots.desc: The shop of Alola Foundation, Timor-Leste's non-governmental organisation for women and children. You can find at Mercado Lama (Mascarenhas) a lot of quality handicrafts produced by weavers from all around Timor-Leste. Bags, wallet, shoes, clothing and various other local handicrafts (all materials made from Tais) and Timorese coffee. A nice souvenir or gift for people at home and you can are…

spots.name: Audian
spots.desc: This area is good for small supermarkets and hardware/household stores. You will need to visit multiple places to find what you want.

spots.name: Leader
spots.desc: Probably the best supermarket for expats, including a lot of household goods.

spots.name: Pateo
spots.desc: Portuguese supermarket. Nicely air-conditioned, unlike most supermarkets here. Good for Portuguese goods, e.g., canned fish, cheese, chorizo, wine, beer. However, it's quite expensive.

spots.name: Lita
spots.desc: The best downtown supermarket. A fruit market is directly opposite.

spots.name: Kmanek
spots.desc: Good cheap downtown supermarket but a limited range. Usually has fruit and veg sellers outside.

spots.name: New Lili's
spots.desc: Good Indonesian warung. Prices have increased since they became popular.

spots.name: Bebonuk beach BBQs
spots.desc: This is a string of identical BBQs that sets up every evening on the beach, serving excellent chicken, pork and fish skewers for about $1 each (they may try to overcharge foreigners) as well as katapas (rice cooked in coconut milk). Gets very messy but it is surely the best value beach dinner in Dili. The stalls set up low tables and chairs straight on the beach.

spots.name: Miaow
spots.desc: Fresly baked French baguettes, develish fillings, mayo "to die for", delicious coffee, evil juices and more!

spots.name: Castaway
spots.desc: One of the hippest and most reliable western joints. Good food, good staff, good crowd and views over the water.

spots.name: Timor Plaza
spots.desc: Has a food court with western and Asian dishes, at higher prices than elsewhere. Makanan, the Indian-Malay place with roti canai, martabak and briyani, may be the best option (Il Gelato is in the same shop, with the best ice cream in Dili). There is a Gloria Jean's with reliable coffee but terrible breakfasts. Elsewhere in Timor Plaza are some cafes, a donut shop and a rooftop restaurant.

spots.name: Queen Tundriee
spots.desc: It can't decide on how to spell tandoori (you'll see tundriee, tundaree, tanduree, tondroori and others), but they know how to do it. Excellent tandoori chicken, samosas and daals, plus many other dishes, including great vegetable dishes.

spots.name: Linivon
spots.desc: Rendang. It's self-service, so you can pick the best pieces. Also has extensive other offerings.

spots.name: New 88
spots.desc: Also has a branch at Landmark and maybe others. Best Chinese food in town according to many Chinese, reliable place to get duck, but relatively expensive for Dili.

spots.name: Caz Bar
spots.desc: Great for drinks or food on the beach (just find the plastic tables and chairs on the sand, or ask staff to get some for you; the main bar is across the road and under cover). Big menu of mostly-western items that are good value considering the location and quality.

spots.name: Kathy's Cafe
spots.desc: Part of Beachside Hotel, it's the other western place on the Areia Branca. Excellent breakfasts eaten on the sand.

spots.name: Early Sun
spots.desc: Reliable Chinese restaurant on the beachfront with a big menu of good-value dishes.

spots.name: Little Pattaya
spots.desc: Combination Thai/Lebanese restaurant. Not the greatest food but probably the nicest setting of the beachfront restaurants and great for groups.

spots.name: Gion
spots.desc: Best Japanese restaurant in town, but be careful about the sashimi.
spots.addr: Timor Plaza, lower level next to the car park

spots.name: Arriba
spots.desc: A good opportunity to savour some of the worst Mexican food in the world. Very bland, poorly-made and quite expensive. Despite being the only Mexican option in town, still doesn't seem to get much business.

spots.name: Golden Star
spots.desc: Attractive Chinese restaurant in the suburbs with a few interesting "Timorese" dishes, like the saboco fish dish.

spots.name: Dilicious Timor
spots.desc: Tasty Timorese food made from local ingredients. Several vegetarian options.

spots.name: Osteria
spots.desc: The best Italian food in town, but that's not saying much. Due to the high prices, the popular Sunday night specials ($10 pizzas and pastas) are the best bet.

spots.name: Panorama
spots.desc: Excellent views over Dili but disappointing food for the price. Just drink at the bar and get some satay sticks instead.

spots.name: Kaliber 12
spots.desc: 24 jam! This corner store blasts music 24 hours a day. You can buy a beer at shop prices, sit outside and meet locals.

spots.name: Tower
spots.desc: One of the hippest bars in town, it fills up with locals and expats (especially Portuguese) from about 23:00. $5 cover charge includes a drink. It's partly outdoors but still fills with cigarette smoke.

spots.name: Moon Bar
spots.desc: The bar that the UN banned its staff from going to! It must be good then, but can you actually find it?

spots.name: Letefoho Specialty Coffee Roasters
spots.desc: Promoting local coffee growers in a small hipster cafe. Some of the best coffee in town.

spots.name: Colmera
spots.desc: This area has a number of electronic and general stores.
spots.addr: Near corner of Rua Nicolau dos Reis Lobato and Estrada de Balidae (aka Colmera Road)

spots.name: Kmanek
spots.desc: Good value but a limited range.

spots.name: W Four
spots.desc: Asian-orientated place but a good range and good prices.

spots.name: Landmark
spots.desc: Large supermarket but lacking many items.

spots.name: Dilimart
spots.desc: Big supermarket downtown.

spots.name: Starco Cafe
spots.desc: Good Indonesian warung.

spots.name: Tito's
spots.desc: Upmarket Portuguese restaurant on the beach.

spots.name: Dominican Café
spots.desc: A cafe in Pante Macassar that offers various drinks, mostly known for its juices. Has a nice courtyard.
spots.price: $1.5 for a juice and $2 for an ice cream cone from the freezer.

spots.name: Old Town
spots.desc: Take a walk around the colonial centre of town. The abandoned and often scorched buildings are eerie reminders of a bygone era. Many of the buildings still have architectural value, particularly the Municipal Market building (dating from 1934) and the salmon-pink Pousada de Baucau. Children play in the buildings and in the fountains and spring overflow. Walk down the road following the beautiful…

spots.name: Piscina de Baucau
spots.desc: A large spring-fed pool owned by the Pousada, set in lush grounds, with a diving board and a slide. Beautiful place for a swim.
spots.hours: Not open Mon & Thu (pool is drained and refilled on those days)

spots.name: Coconut Beach
spots.desc: Beautiful and popular white sand beach with bungalows and camping.

spots.name: Convent
spots.desc: Visit the convent mission for a look at the valuable work the sisters are doing with the children and less fortunate of Baucau. They also have a small store with local handicrafts.

spots.name: Pousada de Baucau
spots.desc: The restaurant at the Pousada aims for a fancy Portuguese and European menu but is very unreliable.

spots.name: Victoria Cafe
spots.desc: Decent restaurant in a nice colonial building with views over the old town. Portuguese and Indonesian.

spots.name: Amalia
spots.desc: Good Indonesian restaurant with a large treed terrace.
spots.addr: down a sort of bridge near the bus stop and market

spots.name: Baucau Beach Bungalows
spots.desc: It also has a restaurant on the beach.

spots.name: Vila Maumeta
spots.desc: Vila is the island's main town, located on the southeast coast. It's home to government offices and NGOs. Around 1,800 people live in this idyllic village with its unpaved streets lined with vibrant red flowers. Cars? A rare sight. Many of the numerous cooperatives sell their products here. Boneca sells unique dolls, and Biojoia sells jewelry. The women earn their living with their handcrafted…

spots.name: Diving on Atauro
spots.desc: Operators arrange dives around Atauro’s coral reefs, plus snorkeling trips and courses.

spots.name: Restaurante Maliana
spots.desc: Pleasant restaurant that typically has a watery curry or stew plus local favourites like liver, beef rendang and vegetable dishes.

spots.name: Laduena
spots.desc: A somewhat larger and more Indonesian menu than the one next door, with beef, chicken and vegetable dishes in the window, plus some à la carte choices.

spots.name: Ave Maria Church
spots.desc: Just about completed, this is the most striking building in Suai and replaces the one that was destroyed in the 1999 massacre by pro-Indonesian militiamen.

spots.name: Eastern Dragon
spots.desc: Bland Chinese food plus a pool table and a herd of bug-eating cats.

spots.name: Restaurante
spots.desc: Only warung in this part of town and offers an alternative to Eastern Dragon. Good chicken and beef but limited veges, although you can get a basic soup to go with it. English-speaking staff.

spots.name: Several basic warungs are in the market
Balibo Flag House
spots.desc: The house in which the five journalists were staying when they were killed by the Indonesian military. The Australian flag they had painted on the wall to avoid being targeted can still be seen. Inside is a small exhibition on the journalists and the incident.

spots.name: Gruta Morutau
spots.desc: A small Lourdes Grotto, outdoor church, and cross, with great views over Balibó and all the way into Indonesia.

spots.name: Balibo Fort Veteran's Museum
spots.desc: An exhibition on the Timorese struggle for independence, the Indonesian invasion, and the international involvement.

spots.name: Restaurant at Balibó Fort Hotel
spots.desc: Relatively fancy restaurant with quiet outdoor seating, views all the way to the sea, serving Pizza, and a number of Asian and international dishes.

spots.name: Tutuala church
spots.desc: The tower of the small village church has a roof similar to a uma lulik, a native holy house that is also one of the national symbols.

spots.name: Ile Kére Kére and O Hi caves
spots.desc: These limestone caves have paintings that are estimated to be 2000-6000 years old, it hasn't been possible to confirm their age. The paintings show hunting scenes, animist symbols - turtles in particular, boats and handprints. The depicted boats are of Austronesian type so it's unclear if the creators have painted their own boats or boats they've seen passing by. There are also pictures of horses…

spots.name: Lena Hara Cave
spots.desc: Further south from the former and along the road to the beach, discovered in 1963. In this cave there's a 10000 year old engraving depicting a human face and scientists have found evidence of the cave being inhabited about 30,000-35,000 years ago.

spots.name: Jerimalai cave
spots.desc: In 2006 scientists discovered remains of human inhabitation that are at least 42,000 years old. This discovery supports the theory that modern humans migrated to Australia through the Lesser Sunda Islands.

spots.name: Old fortifications
spots.desc: Once the Fataluku people built several fortifications (lata irinu) around their settlements in the region. Walls and foundations of these still remain here and there. Right in Tutuala are remains of the Haro fortification, a bit to the west Lochami. At Ile Kére Kére is Mua Mimiraka, and at Lena Hara Ili Mimiraka. Other fortifications include Lorilata, Tutunchau and Upper and Lower Lopomalai.

spots.name: Jaco Island and Valu Beach
spots.desc: Valu Beach with its white sands is a tropical dream, and the same goes for the beach at the adjacent Jaco Island. Jaco is a holy place that one formerly could not visit, nowadays fishermen can take you there for a few dollars. It's also possible to go fishing with them. The sea is excellent for snorkeling. Totems on Valu Beach reveal that this too is a holy place. Despite the fact that East Timor…

spots.name: Mechi celebrations
spots.desc: The Valu Beach is the venue for the Mechi celebrations, related to beginning of the harvest season. The smaller Mechi kiik is celebrated at the last moon quarter in February and the larger Mechi boot at new moon in March. During this time of the year, palolo worms (mechi in the local language) are collected, or rather their reproductive organs that the worms release. They are marinated with chili…
